reasons.text: Investor N's convertible note is fully repaid: 1x its principal plus accrued interest, $268,739.73, paid ahead of all equity as debt. Above this exit value, the next dollar goes to the preference tier Series A Preferred.

The preference tier Series A Preferred is fully paid ($4,000,000.00). Above this exit value, the next dollar goes to the next tier's preference (Seed Preferred, Investor X's SAFE (its Cash-Out Amount) and Investor S's SAFE (its Cash-Out Amount)).
Common starts to be paid here, so the 30,000 options with no strike, such as RSUs, start paying: above this exit value each gets what a common share does.

The preference tier Seed Preferred, Investor X's SAFE (its Cash-Out Amount) and Investor S's SAFE (its Cash-Out Amount) is fully paid ($3,425,000.00). Above this exit value, the next dollar goes to the residual, shared as common.

Common reaches $0.08 per share, the strike on the 150,000 options at that price. Above this exit value they are in the money and exercised: their holders pay the strike, which is added to the proceeds, and share in the residual as common.

Common reaches $0.10 per share, the strike on the 100,000 options at that price. Above this exit value they are in the money and exercised: their holders pay the strike, which is added to the proceeds, and share in the residual as common.

Investor N's convertible note switches from repayment to conversion. Its principal plus interest, $268,739.73, converts at $0.607857 a share (the $10,000,000.00 cap ÷ 16,451,250 shares) into 442,110.44 shares. Here each is worth $0.607857, $268,739.73 in all, which equals its $268,739.73 repayment. Below this exit value repayment pays more; above it, converting does.

Each Seed Preferred share is now worth $1.00, the strike on the warrant for 100,000 Seed Preferred shares. Above this exit value the warrant is in the money and exercised: its holder pays the strike, which is added to the proceeds, and the new shares join Seed Preferred, with its preference and conversion rights.

Seed Preferred converts to common: with the SAFEs paid as their terms then pay them, converting pays it more above this exit value. Converting puts it in the SAFEs' Liquidity Capitalization, so Investor X's SAFE and Investor S's SAFE then take their Conversion Amounts. At this exit value its as-converted share that way (3,781,250 common shares at $0.8000 each = $3,025,000.00) equals its 1x preference of $3,025,000.00; below it, staying preferred pays more.

Investor X's SAFE switches from its Cash-Out Amount to its Conversion Amount, following Seed Preferred: its Liquidity Capitalization now counts it, so its 339,855.66 conversion shares ($250,000.00 ÷ the Liquidity Price of $0.735606) are worth $0.800000 each just above this exit value, $271,884.53 in all, more than its $250,000.00 purchase amount.

Investor S's SAFE switches from its Cash-Out Amount to its Conversion Amount, following Seed Preferred: its Liquidity Capitalization now counts it, so its 339,855.66 conversion shares ($250,000.00 ÷ the Liquidity Price of $0.735606) are worth $0.800000 each just above this exit value, $271,884.53 in all, more than its $250,000.00 purchase amount.
Some payouts jump at this exit value instead of bending, because the decision changes all at once. At exactly this exit value the outcome from below still applies; the jump happens just above it.

Series A Preferred reaches its cap: preference plus participation totals 3x its original issue price ($12,000,000.00). Above this exit value its payout stays flat until converting to common pays more.

Series A Preferred converts to common. At this exit value its as-converted share (2,000,000 common shares at $6.0000 each = $12,000,000.00) equals its capped payout of $12,000,000.00 (3x its original issue price). Below it, staying preferred pays more; above it, converting pays more.
